newsitem.title: USA: Rubin says no sign U.S. inflation re-igniting.
newsitem.headline: Rubin says no sign U.S. inflation re-igniting.

text.p: The U.S. economy is growing solidly with no sign that inflation is at risk of re-igniting, Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Friday.

Speaking to a reporter at a ceremony in his office to introduce a new series of two-dollar bill, Rubin said reports showing low consumer price rises in August and modestly higher retail sales showed "the outlook is very good" for the economy.
"They reinforced the idea...that inflation is not re-igniting, we have solid growth, low inflation, and I think these numbers prove it," Rubin said.
Rubin added that "obviously we have to remain watchful" but that prospects for continued expansion were good.

Earlier, the government reported that the Consumer Price Index rose a slight 0.1 percent in August, while retail sales went up a modest 0.2 percent. The news triggered bond and stock market rallies on hopes that the Federal Reserve might see no need to raise interest rates.
Rubin was presented with a copy of a new series of two-dollar bill that bears his signature. It is not yet in circulation.
The two-dollar bill has not been printed since 1979. The Federal Reserve requested a printing because its supplies were running low.
